summary:
EXOBASE is a web-based platform developed to identify and compare Earth locations that resemble selected regions on the Moon and Mars. It integrates planetary terrain datasets from NASA missions, including LOLA and MOLA, with Earth elevation data to analyze measurable surface characteristics such as elevation, slope, terrain roughness, and local relief.

The platform uses an explainable weighted similarity analysis algorithm to calculate similarity scores and rank potential Earth analog sites for selected planetary regions. It presents the results through interactive maps, comparison tables, visualizations, and dataset provenance information.

EXOBASE addresses the challenge of finding suitable terrestrial analog environments by moving beyond visual comparisons and using quantitative terrain-based analysis. It is important because Earth analog sites help researchers and mission teams study planetary-like environments, plan exploration activities, and prepare for future Moon and Mars missions. The platform provides a systematic, transparent, and expandable approach to planetary analog discovery.
details:
EXOBASE: AI-Powered Planetary Analog Discovery and Mission Site Suitability Assessment is a web-based platform that helps identify Earth locations with terrain characteristics similar to selected regions on the Moon and Mars. It aims to support planetary exploration research by providing a systematic and data-driven way to discover and compare terrestrial analog environments.

1. What does the project do and how does it work?

EXOBASE allows users to select a region on the Moon or Mars and discover Earth locations with similar terrain characteristics. The platform integrates elevation datasets from Earth and NASA planetary missions, including LOLA (Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter) and MOLA (Mars Global Surveyor).

It extracts four terrain features: elevation, slope, surface roughness, and local relief. These features are normalized and compared using an explainable weighted multi-criteria similarity analysis algorithm based on weighted Euclidean distance. The system calculates relative similarity scores and ranks Earth analog candidates.

Users can explore the results through interactive maps, comparison tables, similarity rankings, charts, and detailed dataset information. The current implementation focuses on terrain-based comparison, with thermal and surface-property datasets planned for future integration.

2. What are its benefits?

  • Identifies potential Earth analog environments systematically.
  • Reduces dependence on subjective visual comparisons.
  • Provides measurable and explainable similarity rankings.
  • Integrates datasets from multiple planetary missions.
  • Makes complex terrain information accessible through an interactive interface.
  • Maintains dataset provenance and extraction details for transparency.

3. What is the intended impact?

EXOBASE aims to support researchers, students, and planetary science enthusiasts in exploring terrestrial environments that may serve as analogs for lunar and Martian terrain. It can contribute to preliminary exploration research, analog site identification, mission preparation, and educational activities. It is intended as a research-support tool rather than a replacement for expert geological assessment or actual landing-site safety analysis.

4. What tools and technologies were used?

Programming and data processing:

  • Python
  • JavaScript / TypeScript
  • HTML and CSS
  • NumPy and Pandas
  • Rasterio and GDAL
  • Scikit-learn for supporting data-processing utilities

Datasets and sources:

  • Copernicus DEM GLO-90 for Earth elevation
  • NASA LOLA for lunar topography
  • NASA MOLA for Martian topography

Development and visualization:

  • React-based web frontend
  • Backend APIs for dataset retrieval and similarity analysis
  • Interactive mapping and data visualization libraries
  • Git and GitHub for version control

The project is software-based and does not require dedicated physical hardware.

5. How is the project creative and innovative?

The creative aspect of EXOBASE is its integration of Earth, Moon, and Mars terrain information into a single comparative discovery platform. Instead of simply displaying planetary images, it converts terrain measurements into comparable features and uses an explainable mathematical method to identify and rank potential analog locations. It also emphasizes transparency by displaying dataset sources, spatial resolutions, extraction status, and the features influencing each comparison.

6. What factors did the team consider?

The team considered:

  • Reliability and scientific provenance of datasets.
  • Differences in spatial resolution between planetary datasets.
  • Consistent terrain feature definitions and spatial sampling.
  • Differences in planetary coordinate systems and elevation reference datums.
  • Missing data and incompatible measurements.
  • Fair feature normalization and weighting.
  • Interpretability of similarity scores.
  • Scalability for adding thermal and surface-property datasets.
  • Usability, accessibility, and clarity of the interface.

By combining planetary datasets, geospatial processing, and explainable similarity analysis, EXOBASE provides a transparent foundation for discovering and studying potential Earth analog environments.
